headline: Every tray of meat checked, not a sample.
formProduct: Fresh beef, lamb and pork in sealed trays
label: #FFFFFF
visitLine: Call and visit to one of your plants
heroLede: With fresh meat for hundreds of stores packed across your plants every day, a lifted seal or a wrong label goes straight to the shelf. Here's what a camera check could look like on your tray lines. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every tray has its film on, sealed all the way round, with no meat caught in the seal. A leaking tray of raw meat comes back as a store complaint.
labelLede: Beef mince and lamb mince look much the same through the film. The camera checks every tray carries the right label for the product, straight and intact, so the shopper gets what the label says.
codeLede: Fresh meat has a short shelf life, so the use-by date has to be right on every tray. The system reads the printed date and batch code and compares them with the product and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Glove pieces, blue plastic and tray offcuts are all close at hand in a meat packing plant. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a crate.

vocab.c1h: Film on and sealed all round
vocab.alert: Four creased seals in fifteen minutes on Line 1. Check the tray sealer.
